question: Henry decides one morning to do a workout, and he walks \(\tfrac{3}{4}\) of the way from his home to his gym. The gym is \(2\) kilometers away from Henry’s home. At that point, he changes his mind and walks \(\tfrac{3}{4}\) of the way from where he is back toward home. When he reaches that point, he changes his mind again and walks \(\tfrac{3}{4}\) of the distance from there back toward the gym. If Henry keeps changing his mind when he has walked \(\tfrac{3}{4}\) of the distance toward either the gym or home from the point where he last changed his mind, he will get very close to walking back and forth between a point \(A\) kilometers from home and a point \(B\) kilometers from home. What is \(|A-B|?\)
solution:
Walking \(\tfrac34\) of the way toward a destination leaves \(\tfrac14\) of the original distance to that destination. Combining one gymward walk with one homeward walk gives a useful recurrence.

Let \(a_k\) be Henry's distance from home after his \(k\)th gymward walk, and let \(b_k\) be his distance from home after his \(k\)th homeward walk. Set \(b_0=0\). Then
\[
a_k=b_{k-1}+\frac34(2-b_{k-1})
=\frac32+\frac14b_{k-1}.
\]
On the following homeward walk, he keeps one-quarter of this distance from home, so
\[
b_k=\frac14a_k=\frac38+\frac1{16}b_{k-1}.
\]
Starting from \(b_0=0\), repeated substitution gives
\[
b_k=\frac38\left(1+\frac1{16}+\cdots+\left(\frac1{16}\right)^{k-1}\right).
\]
Since the common ratio \(\tfrac1{16}\) is less than \(1\), the homeward stopping points approach
\[
B=\frac{\tfrac38}{1-\tfrac1{16}}
=\frac38\cdot\frac{16}{15}=\frac25.
\]
The gymward stopping points therefore approach
\[
A=\frac32+\frac14B
=\frac32+\frac1{10}=\frac85.
\]
Hence
\[
|A-B|=\frac85-\frac25=\boxed{\frac65\text{ kilometers}},
\]
which is \(1\tfrac15\) kilometers, choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
